_about: The Rig Card's own words for CastAI's library: each knot's and cast's name, one line, and the one mistake that makes it fail, which group it sits in, the guide titles, and which CastAI fish fills which Fish tab page. These are not corrections (CastAI keeps its own voice). Facts stay CastAI's; a wrong fact is fixed in castai-library-overrides.json, never here. Used by scripts/import-castai-library.mjs.
firstKnotsLine: Spool up, braid to leader, jig on, dropper.

knotGroups.label: Line to line
knotGroups.line: Braid to leader, line to line

knotGroups.label: Hook and lure
knotGroups.line: Line to a hook, jig, lure or swivel

knotGroups.label: Loops
knotGroups.line: A loop at the end or in the middle

improved-clinch.name: Improved clinch
improved-clinch.line: The workhorse. Line to hook, swivel or snap.
improved-clinch.fails: Pulled tight dry, it burns and slips. Wet it first.

palomar.name: Palomar
palomar.line: Strong and fast. The best knot for braid to a hook or jig.
palomar.fails: The loop has to pass over the whole hook or lure. If it catches on the eye, start over.

uni.name: Uni knot
uni.line: One knot for hooks, swivels and the spool.
uni.fails: Braid with too few wraps slips out. Give braid 8 wraps.

blood-knot.name: Blood knot
blood-knot.line: Joins two lines of about the same size.
blood-knot.fails: Both tags must come out of the middle gap from opposite sides, or it pulls apart.

surgeons-knot.name: Surgeon's knot
surgeons-knot.line: The easy way to join a leader, even a different size.
surgeons-knot.fails: Pull all four ends at once. Pull two and it cinches lopsided and weak.

perfection-loop.name: Perfection loop
perfection-loop.line: A small loop that sits straight in line, for loop to loop.
perfection-loop.fails: The tag has to stay pinched between the two loops while you pull through.

dropper-loop.name: Dropper loop
dropper-loop.line: A loop that stands out from the middle of the line, for a second jig or hook.
dropper-loop.fails: Too few twists and the loop pulls out. Twist 5 to 6 times and hold the gap open with a pen.

snell-knot.name: Snell knot
snell-knot.line: Line wrapped down the hook shank, for bait. The hook sets straighter.
snell-knot.fails: The line must leave the eye on the hook point side, or the hook will not turn in.

alberto-knot.name: Alberto knot
alberto-knot.line: Braid to leader, slim enough to cast through the guides.
alberto-knot.fails: Crossed, sloppy wraps make a fat knot that catches the guides. Lay them side by side.

double-uni.name: Double uni
double-uni.line: Braid to leader. Two uni knots slid together.
double-uni.fails: Same wraps on both sides and the braid slips. Give the braid 8, the leader 5.

trilene-knot.name: Trilene knot
trilene-knot.line: A clinch with two turns through the eye. Extra grip on mono.
trilene-knot.fails: Both passes through the eye must go the same way.

surgeons-loop.name: Surgeon's loop
surgeons-loop.line: The fastest loop at the end of a line.
surgeons-loop.fails: Pass the loop through twice. Once is a plain overhand loop and it slips.

non-slip-loop.name: Non slip loop
non-slip-loop.line: Leaves an open loop so a jig or lure swings free.
non-slip-loop.fails: The tag must go back through the overhand on the same side it came out.

davy-knot.name: Davy knot
davy-knot.line: Tiny and fast, for flies and small hooks.
davy-knot.fails: Not a big fish knot. For a big fish, tie a Palomar.

figure-eight-loop.name: Figure eight loop
figure-eight-loop.line: A loop you can check by eye: it looks like an 8.
figure-eight-loop.fails: If it is a blob and not an 8, untie it and start again.

san-diego-jam.name: San Diego jam
san-diego-jam.line: A strong lure knot with extra wraps, good on braid.
san-diego-jam.fails: Wraps that cross or bunch weaken it. Snug the coil neat before you pull tight.

berkley-braid-knot.name: Berkley braid knot
berkley-braid-knot.line: Berkley's hook knot for slippery braid.
berkley-braid-knot.fails: Eight wraps, then the loop goes through the gap by the eye. Miss the gap and it pulls out.

rapala-knot.name: Rapala knot
rapala-knot.line: A loop knot that lets a plug or crankbait swim.
rapala-knot.fails: The last pass goes back through the loop it just made. Skip it and the knot slips.

egg-loop-knot.name: Egg loop
egg-loop-knot.line: A snell with a loop that clamps roe or yarn on the hook.
egg-loop-knot.fails: The tag goes back through the eye the same way it went in, or the wraps slide off.

circle-hook-snell.name: Circle hook snell
circle-hook-snell.line: A snell for circle hooks, so the fish hooks itself.
circle-hook-snell.fails: Do not set the hook hard. Just reel.

fg-knot.name: FG knot
fg-knot.line: The slimmest braid to leader knot. Takes practice.
fg-knot.fails: Slack braid lets the wraps slide off. Keep it tight the whole time.

albright-knot.name: Albright knot
albright-knot.line: Light line or braid to a heavy leader. Tough.
albright-knot.fails: The wraps must stay snug and side by side as you slide them down the loop.

bristol-knot.name: Bristol knot
bristol-knot.line: A heavy leader to a doubled main line.
bristol-knot.fails: It needs a doubled line. Tie a Bimini twist first.

slim-beauty.name: Slim beauty
slim-beauty.line: A heavy leader or bite tippet to lighter line, slim through the guides.
slim-beauty.fails: Wet it and pull slowly. Snatched tight, the wraps cross and it slips.

spider-hitch.name: Spider hitch
spider-hitch.line: A quick double line at the end of the main line.
spider-hitch.fails: Let the wraps come off your thumb one at a time, or they tangle.

bimini-twist.name: Bimini twist
bimini-twist.line: A long doubled line for big fish and heavy leaders.
bimini-twist.fails: Count 20 twists. Fewer and it is weak.

rapala-loop.name: Rapala loop
rapala-loop.line: The Rapala knot, as fly anglers call it.
rapala-loop.fails: The last pass goes back through the loop it just made. Skip it and the knot slips.

bobber-stop-knot.name: Bobber stop knot
bobber-stop-knot.line: A sliding stop that sets how deep a slip float fishes.
bobber-stop-knot.fails: Too few wraps and it slides on the cast. Wrap 3 to 4 times and pull it tight.

nail-knot.name: Nail knot
nail-knot.line: Fly line to backing, or a leader to fly line.
nail-knot.fails: Wraps that cross make a lump that catches the guides. Lay them side by side.

arbor-knot.name: Arbor knot
arbor-knot.line: Ties new line to the reel's spool.
arbor-knot.fails: No stopper knot on the tag and it slips round the spool. Tie both overhands.

haywire-twist.name: Haywire twist
haywire-twist.line: Wire leader to a hook or swivel, for toothy fish.
haywire-twist.fails: Cut the tag with pliers and it leaves a sharp burr. Snap it off.

figure-eight-knot.name: Figure eight stopper
figure-eight-knot.line: A stopper at the end of a rope or line. Will not slip through.
figure-eight-knot.fails: If it does not look like an 8, it is an overhand. Untie it and tie it again.

anchor-hitch.name: Anchor hitch
anchor-hitch.line: Anchor line to the anchor ring or chain.
anchor-hitch.fails: One turn on the ring saws through. Take two.

bowline.name: Bowline
bowline.line: A loop in a rope that will not slip. For the anchor float.
bowline.fails: Slack, it can shake loose. Lock the end.

pendulum-cast.name: Pendulum cast
pendulum-cast.line: The pier swing: an underhand swing out over the rail.
pendulum-cast.fails: Let go late and the rig drops at your feet. Let go as the swing comes up.

overhead-cast.name: Overhead cast
overhead-cast.line: The everyday cast. Straight back, let go at ten o'clock.
overhead-cast.fails: Let go early and it sails up. Let go late and it slaps down at your feet.

sidearm-cast.name: Sidearm cast
sidearm-cast.line: Low and flat, under branches and docks.
sidearm-cast.fails: The rod tip rising sends it up into the trees. Keep it level.

lob-cast.name: Lob cast
lob-cast.line: A gentle underhand toss for bait, close in.
lob-cast.fails: Too light a bait will not carry. It needs some weight.

kayak-cast.name: Kayak cast
kayak-cast.line: Short, low casts from the seat.
kayak-cast.fails: Big wind ups rock the boat. Keep it compact and stay centered.

pitching.name: Pitching
pitching.line: Underhand, lure in your free hand, a quiet entry 10 to 30 feet out.
pitching.fails: Hooks in your palm. Hold the lure by the body, points away.

flipping.name: Flipping
flipping.line: Straight down into heavy cover from a few feet away.
flipping.fails: The bite comes on the fall. Watch the line as it sinks.

pitch-flip.name: Pitch and flip
pitch-flip.line: Both close range moves, for pockets and pilings.
pitch-flip.fails: A splash spooks the fish. Feather the line so the lure slips in.

skip-cast.name: Skip cast
skip-cast.line: Skip the lure like a stone, back under docks.
skip-cast.fails: Too steep and it digs in instead of skipping. Keep it low and flat.

bow-and-arrow-cast.name: Bow and arrow cast
bow-and-arrow-cast.line: Pull the lure back and let the rod shoot it. For tiny gaps.
bow-and-arrow-cast.fails: Never hold it by the hooks. Hold the body.

roll-cast.name: Roll cast
roll-cast.line: A fly cast with no back cast. Rolls the line off the water.
roll-cast.fails: No pause, no D loop, no cast. Let the line hang behind the rod first.

double-haul.name: Double haul
double-haul.line: Pull the fly line on both strokes for more distance.
double-haul.fails: Haul only while the rod moves fast. Early or late kills the cast.

water-haul.name: Water haul
water-haul.line: Let the water load the rod when there is no room behind.
water-haul.fails: Do not pause after you rip the line off. Go forward at once.

two-handed-spey-cast.name: Spey cast
two-handed-spey-cast.line: Two handed rod, big rivers, no back cast.
two-handed-spey-cast.fails: Rushing the pause. Let the rod load before you drive forward.

cutthroat.why: CastAI's habitat is the inland trout of mountain streams; the Rig Card's cutthroat are sea-run, on the Sound's beaches.

perch.why: The Rig Card's perch lakes do not freeze over.
